text: The Koch family is an American family engaged in business, most noted for its political activities and for controlling Koch Industries, the second-largest privately owned company in the United States, which had 2013 revenues of $115 billion.
The Koch family business was started by Fred C. Koch, who developed a new cracking method for the refinement of heavy crude oil into gasoline.
Fred C. Koch's four sons litigated against each other over their interests in the Koch family business during the 1980s and 1990s.
Banfield Pet Hospital is a privately owned company based in Vancouver, Washington, United States, that operates veterinary clinics.
Banfield Pet Hospital is part of the Mars, Incorporated family of companies and owns veterinary clinics in the United States, Mexico, and the United Kingdom.
Founded in 1955, Banfield Pet Hospital operates many of its more than 800 clinics inside PetSmart stores and is the largest privately owned veterinary practice in the United States.
On April 2, 2014, Banfield Pet Hospital announced that its headquarters would relocate to Vancouver, Washington, from nearby Portland, Oregon.
ProSieben is a commercial television station in Germany, largely distributed by cable and satellite and to a lesser extent by digital video broadcasting terrestrial.
ProSieben began operations on 1 January 1989 and is Germany's second-largest privately owned television company.
Since 2003, ProSieben has been part of ProSiebenSat.1 Media, and although ProSieben produces some of its own programming, it also airs many American imports.
ProSieben launched a pay TV channel called ProSieben Fun on 3 May 2012, and a third channel called ProSieben Maxx started broadcasting on 3 September 2013.
The Koch family foundations are a group of charitable foundations in the United States associated with the family of Fred C. Koch.
The most prominent Koch family foundations are the Charles Koch Foundation and the David H. Koch Charitable Foundation, created by Charles Koch and David Koch, two sons of Fred C. Koch.
Charles Koch and David Koch own the majority of Koch Industries, an oil, gas, paper, and chemical conglomerate that is the second-largest privately held company in the United States.

The Charles Koch Foundation and the David H. Koch Charitable Foundation have provided millions of dollars to organizations including libertarian and conservative think tanks, with funding areas including political advocacy, climate change scepticism, higher education scholarships, cancer research, arts, and science.
Dark Money: The Hidden History of the Billionaires Behind the Rise of the Radical Right (2016) is a non-fiction book written by the American investigative journalist Jane Mayer.

Dark Money by Jane Mayer is about a network of extremely wealthy conservative libertarians, foremost among them Charles and David Koch, who have funded organizations that influence academic institutions, think tanks, the courts, statehouses, Congress, and the American presidency.
Jane Mayer's book Dark Money also discusses Richard Mellon Scaife and John M. Olin, who funded the American Legislative Exchange Council (ALEC), as well as the DeVos and Coors families.
New Zealand Mint, whose Maori name is Te Kamupene Whakanao o Aotearoa, is a privately owned company in Auckland, New Zealand, and it is the only privately owned mint in New Zealand.
New Zealand Mint, a privately owned company in Auckland, purchases refined gold from international sources to produce its coins.
New Zealand Mint trades in precious metals including gold bullion and also operates as a physical storage provider.
Fred Chase Koch (September 23, 1900 to November 17, 1967) was an American chemical engineer and entrepreneur.
Fred Chase Koch founded the oil refinery firm that later became Koch Industries, a privately held company under the principal ownership and leadership of his sons Charles and David.
Forbes lists Koch Industries, as of 2015, as the second-largest privately held company in the United States.
Minnetonka is a suburban city in Hennepin County, Minnesota, United States, located eight miles (13 km) west of Minneapolis.
Minnetonka had a population of 49,734 at the 2010 census, and its name comes from the Dakota Indian phrase mni tanka, meaning great water.
The city of Minnetonka is the home of Cargill, the country's largest privately owned company, and United Healthcare, the state's largest publicly owned company.
New York State Route 9N (NY 9N) is a north-south state highway in northeastern New York in the United States.
NY 9N extends from an intersection with US 9, NY 29, and NY 50 in the city of Saratoga Springs to a junction with US 9 and NY 22 in the Clinton County hamlet of Keeseville.

At 143.49 miles in total length, NY 9N is the longest letter-suffixed route in New York State, and it runs concurrently with US 9 for 1 mile in the village of Lake George and for three blocks in the hamlet of Elizabethtown.

New York State Route 9B (NY 9B) is a state highway located within Clinton County, New York, in the United States, serving as a connector between its parent route US 9 in the town of Champlain and US 11 in the village of Rouses Point.

NY 9B is the northernmost section of the Lakes to Locks Passage, an All-American Road, and it veers east to serve the village and shoreline of Lake Champlain while US 9 bypasses Rouses Point to the west.

Modern NY 9B was the original alignment of US 9 through the town of Champlain; when US 9 was moved onto its present alignment west of Rouses Point in the mid-1940s, its former routing to Rouses Point became NY 9B.
Boght Corners, also referred to as Boght, is a hamlet in the town of Colonie in northern Albany County, New York, that straddles U.S. Route 9.
The corners that give Boght Corners its name are found at the intersection of Route 9 and Boght Road (NY Route 9R on the leg east of the hamlet), near the Boght Community Fire District station.
The Boght Corners hamlet is served by the North Colonie Central School District and contains Boght Hills Elementary School.

Borodino is a hamlet located at the intersection of New York State Route 41 (East Lake Road) and New York State Route 174 (Rose Hill Road) in the Town of Spafford in Onondaga County, New York, near Skaneateles Lake.
A monument for veterans, designed by Gianfranco Fritelli, stands in a cemetery at the southeast corner of the Borodino intersection.

A little-altered Federal style Methodist Church known locally as The Church, dating from 1830, stands close to Route 174 in Borodino, and the Borodino District School No. 8 (c. 1853-59) and Borodino Hall (1835) are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
New York State Route 9R (NY 9R) is a north-south state highway in northeastern Albany County, New York, in the United States, and it is a 3.22 mile eastern loop of US 9.
NY 9R connects US 9 to the city of Cohoes, 1.5 miles to the east, leaving US 9 in the hamlet of Latham and rejoining it in the hamlet of Boght Corners, both located in the town of Colonie.

Most of NY 9R is a two-lane highway passing through residential areas, but its southwesternmost portion is four lanes wide and serves a commercial district; the route was assigned around 1939 and has remained largely unchanged, apart from a brief 1970s period when NY 9R was partially replaced by NY 470.
The Prospect Mountain Veterans Memorial Highway is a 5.88 mile parkway located in the town of Lake George, New York.
The Prospect Mountain Veterans Memorial Highway starts at the concurrency of US 9 and NY 9N and ends at the peak of Prospect Mountain.

Although the Prospect Mountain Veterans Memorial Highway is designated as New York State Route 917A, an unsigned reference route, by the New York State Department of Transportation, all maintenance on the roadway is performed by the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation.
New York State Route 418 (NY 418) is a 3.50 mile state highway located entirely within the Adirondack Park in Warren County, New York, in the United States.

NY 418 begins just west of the hamlet of Thurman Station, where Athol Road changes designations from County Route 4 to NY 418, and heads eastward through the towns of Thurman and Warrensburg, following the Schroon River to US 9 in the hamlet of Warrensburg.
All of NY 418 is part of the Dude Ranch Trail, a New York State Scenic Byway that runs through Warren County and Saratoga County.
New York State Route 9G (NY 9G) is a state highway in the Hudson Valley of New York in the United States that runs north from US 9 at Poughkeepsie, starting out as Violet Avenue.

NY 9G follows the Hudson River mostly along the eastern side of US 9 to Rhinebeck, where the two routes cross just north of the village, then runs on the western side of US 9 to Hudson, ending at another junction with US 9 in the city.

NY 9G initially extended from Rhinebeck to Hudson when it was assigned as part of the 1930 renumbering of New York state highways, and it was extended to its current length in the late 1930s, supplanting New York State Route 9F.
Yonkers Avenue is an east-west street in the city of Yonkers in Westchester County, New York, in the United States, and it is one of four major east-west through routes in the city.
The western terminus of Yonkers Avenue is at Nepperhan Avenue, which connects to US 9 and NY 9A, while its eastern terminus is at Bronx River Road near the Bronx River Parkway.

The New York State Department of Transportation maintains all of Yonkers Avenue as New York State Route 983C from Nepperhan Avenue to the Saw Mill River Parkway and as New York State Route 984E from the Saw Mill Parkway to Bronx River Road, both unsigned reference route designations.

New York State Route 157A (NY 157A) is an east-west state highway located in Albany County, New York, in the United States, serving as a 5.88 mile loop route of NY 157 through the towns of Knox and Berne.
NY 157A veers a considerable distance to the south to serve the hamlet of East Berne and indirectly connects NY 157 to NY 443, then rejoins NY 157 near the access road to Thompson's Lake State Park.
NY 157A is a two-lane highway its entire length and, like its parent route NY 157, was assigned in 1930 to its current routing.
Schapelle Leigh Corby (born 10 July 1977) is an Australian woman who was convicted of smuggling cannabis into Indonesia.
Schapelle Leigh Corby spent nine years imprisoned on the Indonesian island of Bali in Kerobokan Prison.

Since her arrest, Schapelle Leigh Corby has publicly maintained that the drugs were planted in her bodyboard bag and that she did not know about them, and her trial and conviction were a major focus of Australian media attention.
Sinan Tuzcu is a Turkish actor, and his birth date is recorded as 10 July 1977.
The Turkish actor Sinan Tuzcu has Turkish nationality and was born on 10 July 1977.
Solomon Northup (July 10, 1807 or 1808 to 1863) was an American abolitionist and the primary author of the memoir Twelve Years a Slave.

Solomon Northup was a free-born African American from New York, the son of a freed slave and a free woman of color, and he worked as a farmer, a professional violinist, and a landowner in Hebron, New York.

In 1841, Solomon Northup was offered a traveling musician's job and went to Washington, D.C., where slavery was legal; there he was drugged, kidnapped, and sold as a slave, then shipped to New Orleans and held as a slave for 12 years in the Red River region of Louisiana, mostly in Avoyelles Parish.

Solomon Northup regained his freedom on January 3, 1853, after a Canadian working on his plantation helped get word to New York, and his family and friends enlisted the aid of the Governor of New York, Washington Hunt.
João Pereira is a retired Angolan footballer who was born on 10 July 1977 in the city of Benguela.
The last club for which the retired Angolan footballer João Pereira played was Atlético Sport Aviação.
Levan Kobiashvili is a retired Georgian footballer, born on 10 July 1977, and his name is also written in Georgian script.
Levan Kobiashvili is the current president of the Georgian Football Federation, the national football governing body of Georgia.
Travis David Wilson (born 10 July 1977 in Christchurch, New Zealand) is a current member of the Black Socks, New Zealand's national softball team.
Travis David Wilson first played for the Black Socks in 1994 and was an integral part of their ISF Men's World Championship winning team in Midland, Michigan in 1996.
12 Years a Slave is the original soundtrack album to the 2013 film 12 Years a Slave, which starred Chiwetel Ejiofor, Michael Fassbender, Benedict Cumberbatch, Paul Dano, and Lupita Nyong'o.
The 12 Years a Slave soundtrack album contains twenty-one tracks from the original film score written and composed by Hans Zimmer.
The 12 Years a Slave score was widely admired and thought of as a contender for the Academy Award for Original Music Score at the 86th Academy Awards.
José Marcos Garay Álvarez is a Mexican footballer who was born on 10 July 1977 and is still active in the game.
José Marcos Garay Álvarez currently plays as a footballer for the club Tecos in the Mexican First Division.
Chiwetel Umeadi Ejiofor, CBE, is a British actor who was born on 10 July 1977.

After enrolling at the National Youth Theatre in 1995 and gaining a scholarship to the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art, Chiwetel Ejiofor was cast by Steven Spielberg, at age 19 and three months into his course, to play a supporting role as James Covey in the film Amistad (1997).
Javier Lux, born 10 July 1977 in Carcarañá, Santa Fe Province, is a retired Argentine football midfielder.
Javier Lux has a brother, Germán Lux, who is a goalkeeper and has represented Argentina internationally.
The Taj Mahal, whose name means Crown of the Palace, is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna river in the Indian city of Agra.
Shah Jahan, the Mughal emperor who reigned from 1628 to 1658, commissioned the Taj Mahal in 1632 to house the tomb of his favourite wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
The Taj Mahal is the centrepiece of a 42 acre complex that includes a mosque and a guest house, set in formal gardens bounded on three sides by a crenellated wall.
The Taj Mahal Palace Hotel is a Heritage Grand class five-star hotel in the Colaba region of Mumbai, Maharashtra, India, located next to the Gateway of India.
The Taj Mahal Palace Hotel was historically known as the Taj Mahal Hotel or the Taj Palace Hotel, and is also simply called the Taj.
R. Chandru is a Kannada film writer and director who debuted with the successful 2008 film Taj Mahal.
Following the huge success of the 2008 film Taj Mahal, R. Chandru became popularly known as Taj Mahal Chandru in the media.
Kester Smitty Smith is an American percussionist who is the drummer for the Taj Mahal Trio and has collaborated with jazz, blues and world musicians.
Kester Smitty Smith has performed with and alongside the musician Taj Mahal for over forty years.
Kester Smitty Smith has recorded music with Taj Mahal, Geoff Muldaur, Peter Rowan, Cedella Booker, Morgan Freeman, Ellen McIlwaine, Mary Coughlan and Pinetop Perkins.
The replica known as Mini Taj Mahal or Qadri's Taj Mahal, officially named Maqbara Yadgare Mohabbat Tajammuli Begum, is a copy of the historic Taj Mahal of Agra.
The Mini Taj Mahal replica is located in Kaser Kalan, a small village in Bulandshahar of Uttar Pradesh, India.
The Mini Taj Mahal replica was built by 81-year-old retired postmaster Faizul Hasan Qadri in memory of his dead wife Tajamulli Begum, who died of throat cancer in 2011.
Agra Fort is a historical fort in the city of Agra in India, and it was the main residence of the Mughal Dynasty emperors until 1638, when the capital was shifted from Agra to Delhi.
Agra Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage site located about 2.5 km northwest of its more famous sister monument, the Taj Mahal.
Agra Fort can be more accurately described as a walled city than simply as a fort.
Taj Mahal Bangladesh is a scaled copy of the original Taj Mahal, the Mughal mausoleum located in Agra, India, and it sits 10 miles east of the Bangladeshi capital, Dhaka, in Sonargaon.
Unlike the original Taj Mahal, work on the Taj Mahal Bangladesh replica took only five years.

Ahsanullah Moni, a wealthy Bangladeshi film-maker, announced his Copycat version of Taj Mahal project in December 2008; the project cost about USD 56 million and was built 20 miles northeast of Dhaka.

Moni explained that he built the replica so that the poor of his nation could realise their dream of seeing neighbouring India's famed monument, which drew complaints from an Indian High Commission official in Dhaka.

The Black Taj Mahal, also called Black Taj, Kaala Taj, or the 2nd Taj, is a legendary black marble mausoleum said to have been planned to be built across the Yamuna River opposite the Taj Mahal in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India.
Mughal emperor Shah Jahan is said to have desired a mausoleum for himself similar to the one he had built in memory of his third wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
Taj Mahal is a 1963 film based on the historical legend of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.
According to the legend on which the 1963 film Taj Mahal is based, Shah Jahan created the Taj Mahal in fond remembrance and as a tomb for his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal.

The Taj Heritage Corridor case is an alleged scam in which, during 2002-2003, the then Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh Mayawati and a minister in her government, Nasimuddin Siddiqui, were charged with corruption.
The Taj Corridor project was intended to upgrade tourist facilities near the Taj Mahal and was to be implemented during Mayawati's tenure as Chief Minister.

The then BJP government at the Centre gave the Environmental Clearance required for the Taj Corridor project near the Taj Mahal, but the BJP later backed out, said the project was not cleared by the Environment Ministry, and blamed Mayawati for starting construction work near the Taj Mahal.
Ron Bottcher (11 May 1940 to 12 April 1991) was an American operatic baritone and a native of Sandpoint, Idaho.

Ron Bottcher earned music degrees from the University of Montana and the Curtis Institute of Music, and was actively performing with both the New York City Opera and the Metropolitan Opera during the 1960s.

Ron Bottcher made his debut at the Santa Fe Opera in the summer of 1961, portraying Leopold in Richard Strauss's Der Rosenkavalier, Marcello in Giacomo Puccini's La boheme, and the Head waiter in Paul Hindemith's Neues vom Tage.

Ron Bottcher created roles in the world premieres of Samuel Barber's Antony and Cleopatra and Marvin David Levy's Mourning Becomes Electra at the Metropolitan Opera, and he died at age 50 at Lenox Hill Hospital in Manhattan of AIDS related illness.
La bohème, also known as La bohème de Puccini, is a 1988 Italian-French film of an opera directed by Luigi Comencini.
The 1988 film La bohème, directed by Luigi Comencini, is based on Giacomo Puccini's opera La bohème.
Gianni Schicchi is a comic opera in one act by Giacomo Puccini with an Italian libretto by Giovacchino Forzano, composed in 1917-18.

The libretto of Gianni Schicchi is based on an incident mentioned in Dante's Divine Comedy, and the opera is the third and final part of Puccini's Il trittico (The Triptych), three one-act operas with contrasting themes.
Although Gianni Schicchi continues to be performed with one or both of the other trittico operas, it is now more frequently staged either alone or with short operas by other composers.
The aria O mio babbino caro from Gianni Schicchi is one of Puccini's best known arias and one of the most popular arias in opera.
Franco Corelli (8 April 1921 to 29 October 2003) was an Italian tenor who had a major international opera career between 1951 and 1976.

Franco Corelli was associated in particular with the spinto and dramatic tenor roles of the Italian repertory, was celebrated for his powerhouse voice, electrifying top notes, clear timbre and passionate singing, and was dubbed the Prince of tenors.

Franco Corelli had a long and fruitful partnership with the Metropolitan Opera in New York City between 1961 and 1975, and he also appeared on the stages of most of the major opera houses in Europe and with opera companies throughout North America.
O mio babbino caro (Oh My Beloved Father) is a soprano aria from the opera Gianni Schicchi (1918) by Giacomo Puccini, to a libretto by Giovacchino Forzano.

In Gianni Schicchi, O mio babbino caro is sung by Lauretta after tensions between her father Schicchi and the family of Rinuccio, the boy she loves, reach a breaking point that threatens to separate her from Rinuccio.

O mio babbino caro provides an interlude of lyrical simplicity and single-hearted love, in contrast with the hypocrisy, jealousy, double-dealing and feuding of medieval Florence in Puccini's only comedy, and it is the only set-piece in the through-composed opera.
La fanciulla del West (The Girl of the West) is an opera in three acts by Giacomo Puccini to an Italian libretto, based on the play The Girl of the Golden West by the American author David Belasco.
La fanciulla del West followed Madama Butterfly, which was also based on a Belasco play.

La fanciulla del West has fewer of the show-stopping highlights characteristic of other Puccini works, but it is admired for its impressive orchestration and for a score that is more melodically integrated than is typical of Puccini's previous work.

La fanciulla del West displays influences from composers Claude Debussy and Richard Strauss without being in any way imitative, and similarities between its libretto and the work of Richard Wagner have also been found, though some attribute this to the original plot of the play.
Tosca is a 1956 Italian musical film directed by Carmine Gallone and starring Franca Duval, Afro Poli and Franco Corelli.
The 1956 film Tosca is based on the opera Tosca by Giacomo Puccini and was made at Cinecitta in Rome.
The Festival Puccini, also called the Puccini Festival, is an annual summer opera festival held in July and August to present the operas of the Italian composer Giacomo Puccini.
Giacomo Puccini is the famous Italian composer whose operas are presented each summer at the annual Festival Puccini in July and August.
Cesira Ferrani (May 8, 1863 in Turin to May 4, 1943 in Pollone) was an Italian operatic soprano.

Cesira Ferrani is best known for debuting two of the most iconic roles in opera history: Mimi in the original 1896 production of Giacomo Puccini's La boheme, and the title role in Puccini's Manon Lescaut in its 1893 world premiere.
Cesira Ferrani sang a wide repertoire that encompassed verismo opera as well as the works of composers such as Verdi, Gounod, Wagner and Debussy.
Jacopo (Giacomo) Puccini, who lived from 26 January 1712 to 16 May 1781, was an 18th-century Italian composer who lived and worked primarily in Lucca, Tuscany.
Jacopo Puccini was the first of five generations of composers, the most famous of whom was his great-great-grandson, the opera composer Giacomo Puccini.

Giam Siak Kecil-Bukit Batu, officially Cagar Biosfer Giam Siak Kecil Bukit Batu (CB-GSK-BB), is a peatland area in Riau Province of Sumatra covering 705,271 ha across large parts of Bengkalis Regency and Siak Regency.
Giam Siak Kecil-Bukit Batu is a declared UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Reserve that supports a sustainable timber industry.
Giam Siak Kecil-Bukit Batu is home to two wildlife reserves, Giam Siak Wildlife Reserve and Bukit Batu Wildlife Reserve, whose flagship species include the Sumatran elephant and the Sumatran tiger.

Krau Wildlife Reserve is the largest wildlife reserve, covering 60,349 ha, located in the Titiwangsa Mountains in the central state of Pahang, Malaysia, and it was established during the British Colonial Administration.
Krau Wildlife Reserve is managed by the Department of Wildlife and National Parks and is located south of Lanchang township.

In the 1960s, Lord Medway led a zoological expedition to Gunong Benom (2110 m asl), which later attracted many scholars, biologists and primatologists to research the eastern part of Krau Wildlife Reserve, called Kuala Krau.
Project African Wilderness (PAW) is a not for profit organisation with the express purpose of protecting and restoring the Mwabvi Wildlife Reserve in Malawi.
The Mwabvi Wildlife Reserve in Malawi is the reserve targeted for protection and restoration by the not for profit Project African Wilderness.
The Saint-Maurice Wildlife Reserve is a 782 km2 wildlife reserve north of Shawinigan, located west of the Saint-Maurice River in the territory of the Mekinac Regional County Municipality.
Like all wildlife reserves, the Saint-Maurice Wildlife Reserve is dedicated to the conservation, development and use of wildlife as well as the practice of recreational activity.
The Saint-Maurice Wildlife Reserve is not considered a protected area, because forest and mining activities are allowed there.
The Katonga Wildlife Reserve is a wildlife reserve in western Uganda along the banks of the Katonga River, established in 1998 and covering approximately 211 km2.
Many of the plant and animal species in the Katonga Wildlife Reserve are unique to its wetland environment.
Sir Bani Yas is a natural island located 170 km southwest of Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, and it lies 9 km offshore from Jebel Dhanna.
Sir Bani Yas is 17.5 km from north to south and 9 km from east to west, making it the largest natural island in the United Arab Emirates.
Sir Bani Yas was originally home to Arabia's largest wildlife reserve, which spans over 87 km2 and was established in 1977 by Sheikh Zayed Bin Sultan Al Nahyan.

Sir Bani Yas is now home to thousands of large free-roaming animals and several million trees and plants, and it offers activities such as adventure safaris, kayaking, mountain biking, archery, hiking and snorkeling.
The Mastigouche Wildlife Reserve is a Quebec Wildlife Reserve located in the administrative regions of Mauricie and Lanaudiere, Quebec, in Canada.

Like all wildlife reserves, the Mastigouche Wildlife Reserve is dedicated to the conservation, development and use of wildlife as well as recreational activities, but it is not considered a protected area because forest and mining activities are allowed.
The Ferlo Sud Wildlife Reserve, French name Reserve de Faune du Ferlo-Sud, was established in 1972 and is a 6337 km2 IUCN habitat and species protected nature reserve located in Senegal.
The Ferlo Sud Wildlife Reserve in Senegal is bordered to the north by the Ferlo Nord Wildlife Reserve.
Mwabvi Wildlife Reserve, with an area of 135 km2, is Malawi's smallest national park and also its least accessible.
Mwabvi Wildlife Reserve has a wide variety of habitats, including Mopane, Combretum and brachystegia woodland, as well as open savanna, dambo, and riverine areas.

Mwabvi Wildlife Reserve was the last natural home to Malawi's Black Rhino population, but both wildlife and woodland have been poached in recent years, although antelope such as kudu, sable, impala and nyala remain, and leopard and hyena have been seen.

Lions from neighbouring Mozambique are regular visitors to Mwabvi Wildlife Reserve, where buffalo still bathe in the Mwabvi river and the scenery offers views over the Shire River and the Zambesi river.
The African buffalo, or Cape buffalo (Syncerus caffer), is a large African bovine that is not closely related to the slightly larger wild water buffalo of Asia, and its ancestry remains unclear.

Syncerus caffer caffer, the Cape buffalo, is the typical and largest subspecies, found in South and East Africa, while S. c. nanus, the African forest buffalo, is the smallest subspecies, common in forest areas of Central and West Africa.

The adult African buffalo's horns have fused bases forming a continuous bone shield across the top of the head, referred to as a boss, and African buffalo are widely regarded as very dangerous, goring and killing over 200 people every year.
Raptors 905 are a Canadian professional basketball team in the NBA G League, based in Mississauga, Ontario, that began play in the 2015-16 season.

Raptors 905 are the G League affiliate of the Toronto Raptors and play their home games at the Hershey Centre, replacing the Mississauga Power of the National Basketball League of Canada as the Centre's basketball tenant.

Raptors 905 also play occasional home games at the Air Canada Centre, the home of their parent club, and they were the eighth D-League team owned by an NBA team and the first to be based outside the United States.

The Portland Trail Blazers, commonly known as the Blazers, are an American professional basketball team based in Portland, Oregon, that plays in the Northwest Division of the Western Conference of the NBA.

The Portland Trail Blazers originally played home games in the Memorial Coliseum before moving to the Rose Garden in 1995, and the franchise entered the league in 1970 with Portland as its only home city.
From 1977 through 1995, the Portland Trail Blazers sold out 814 consecutive home games, the longest such streak in American major professional sports.

The Portland Trail Blazers are the only team in the major professional North American sports leagues located in the state of Oregon, and they are the only NBA team based in the binational Pacific Northwest, after the Vancouver Grizzlies relocated to Memphis in 2001 and the Seattle SuperSonics relocated to Oklahoma City in 2008.
The Portland Trail Blazers compete in the NBA as a member club of the league's Western Conference Northwest Division and are based in Portland, Oregon.
The Portland Trail Blazers played their home games in the Memorial Coliseum before moving to the Moda Center in 1995, which was called the Rose Garden until 2013.

The Portland Trail Blazers entered the league as an expansion team in 1970 and sold out 814 consecutive home games from 1977 through 1995, the longest such streak in American major professional sports at the time, only since surpassed by the Boston Red Sox.

The Portland Trail Blazers have been the only NBA team based in the bi-national Pacific Northwest since the Vancouver Grizzlies relocated to Memphis in 2001 and the Seattle SuperSonics relocated to Oklahoma City in 2008.
The Long Island Nets are an American professional basketball team of the NBA G League and an affiliate of the Brooklyn Nets of the National Basketball Association.
The Long Island Nets are based in Nassau County and play their home games at the Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum in Uniondale, New York.
The Long Island Nets became the twelfth D-League team to be owned by an NBA team.
The New Orleans Pelicans are an American professional basketball team based in New Orleans, Louisiana, that competes in the NBA as a member club of the league's Western Conference Southwest Division.
The New Orleans Pelicans play their home games in the Smoothie King Center, which was formerly known as the New Orleans Arena.
The Erie BayHawks are an American professional basketball team of the NBA G League and an affiliate of the Atlanta Hawks of the National Basketball Association, based in Erie, Pennsylvania.
The Erie BayHawks will play their home games during the 2017-18 and 2018-19 seasons at the Erie Insurance Arena.
The Atlanta Hawks currently plan to relocate their G League franchise to College Park, Georgia, before the 2019-20 season, to play at a new arena in the Georgia International Convention Center.
The Erie BayHawks became the sixteenth D-League team to be owned by an NBA team.

The Washington NBA G League team is an American professional basketball team in the NBA G League and an affiliate of the Washington Wizards of the National Basketball Association, based in Washington, D.C.
The Washington NBA G League team will play its home games during the 2018-19 season at the St. Elizabeths East Entertainment and Sports Arena.
The Washington NBA G League team became the twenty-third G League team to be owned by an NBA team.

The Windy City Bulls are an American professional basketball team of the NBA G League and an affiliate of the Chicago Bulls of the National Basketball Association, based in northwest-suburban Hoffman Estates, Illinois.
The Windy City Bulls play their home games at the Sears Centre, 25 miles from Chicago, and the team became the thirteenth D-League team to be owned by an NBA team.
The Windy City Bulls are coached by Nate Loenser, a former video coordinator with the Chicago Bulls.
Jalen Jones (born May 27, 1993) is an American professional basketball player for the New Orleans Pelicans of the National Basketball Association.
Jalen Jones was signed on a two-way contract with the NBA G League and played college basketball for Southern Methodist and Texas A&M.
The Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team, formerly the Marquette Warriors, represents Marquette University in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and currently competes in the Big East.
The Marquette Golden Eagles last played in the NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament in 2013 but were selected for the upcoming 2017 tournament.

The Marquette Golden Eagles maintain rivalries with the University of Wisconsin-Madison, the University of Louisville, the University of Notre Dame and DePaul University, and play their home games at the Bradley Center in downtown Milwaukee, where the Milwaukee Bucks also play.
Despite having only 8,000 undergraduates, Marquette University was ranked 10th in average attendance among NCAA Division 1 teams in 2009 and 2010.
Blues Traveler is an American rock band formed in Princeton, New Jersey in 1987, whose music covers a variety of genres including blues rock, psychedelic rock, folk rock, soul and Southern rock.

Blues Traveler is known for its extensive use of segues in live performances and was considered a key part of the re-emerging jam band scene of the 1990s, spearheading the H.O.R.D.E. touring music festival.
Blues Traveler, the eponymous debut album from the band Blues Traveler, was released on A&M Records in 1990.
The Blues Traveler debut album establishes the band's trademark jam band sound, featuring John Popper's harmonica.

Blues Brothers 2000: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack is the third studio album by The Blues Brothers and their twelfth release overall, and it is a soundtrack album to the 1998 film Blues Brothers 2000.
The 1998 film Blues Brothers 2000 is the sequel to the 1980 film The Blues Brothers, and its soundtrack album is the third studio album by The Blues Brothers.

The Blues Brothers 2000 soundtrack includes tracks by the Blues Brothers Band and guest artists such as Aretha Franklin, James Brown, Eddie Floyd and Wilson Pickett, as well as songs by the Paul Butterfield Blues Band and Blues Traveler.

The Blues Brothers 2000 soundtrack also features the all-star blues supergroup the Louisiana Gator Boys, including B.B. King, Eric Clapton, Bo Diddley, Charlie Musselwhite, Doctor John, Lou Rawls, Koko Taylor, Isaac Hayes, Billy Preston and other artists.
North Hollywood Shootout is American jam band Blues Traveler's tenth studio album, released on August 26, 2008.
North Hollywood Shootout, Blues Traveler's tenth studio album, was produced by David Bianco, a 1996 Grammy winner.
In a notable departure from previous Blues Traveler releases, the North Hollywood Shootout album includes a spoken word piece featuring Bruce Willis.
On Tour Forever is a live EP album released by the band Blues Traveler in 1992, and only ten thousand copies were produced.
On Tour Forever was packaged as a double album with copies of Blues Traveler's second album, Travelers and Thieves.
Decipher is the second album by Dutch symphonic metal band After Forever, released in 2001.
On Decipher, After Forever make use of live classical instruments and a complete choir to back up the soprano voice of lead singer Floor Jansen.

Decipher includes a duet of soprano and tenor voices in Imperfect Tenses and a recording of the late Israeli PM Yizhak Rabin's voice during the Peace treaty signing ceremony on October 26, 1994, on the track Forlorn Hope.
Decipher is the last After Forever album with guitarist and founder Mark Jansen, who left the band soon after its release.
Travelers and Thieves is Blues Traveler's second album, released on A&M Records in 1991 in two versions: an album-only version and an extremely limited two-CD pressing.
The bonus disc of the two-CD pressing of Travelers and Thieves was called On Tour Forever.
On iTunes, the Blues Traveler album Travelers and Thieves is listed only as Travelers, because the full name is split across two drawings, one on the cover and one inside the CD liner notes.
Travelogue: Blues Traveler Classics is a compilation album by American rock band Blues Traveler, released in 2002.
Travelogue: Blues Traveler Classics is composed of the band's greatest hits from before they were dropped by A&M Records.
Exordium is a 2003 EP album by Dutch symphonic metal band After Forever, and another version released in 2004 included a bonus DVD entitled Insights.
The Exordium EP includes a cover of the Iron Maiden song The Evil That Men Do, and a metal version of One Day I'll Fly Away, a ballad originally sung by Randy Crawford.
Exordium is the first recording by After Forever with new guitarist Bas Maas, who replaced Mark Jansen.
Exordium is the first After Forever album to enter the Dutch Top 100 chart, where it remained for two weeks, peaking at number 56.
Bridge is the sixth album by American jam band Blues Traveler, released in May 2001, and it was originally titled Bridge Out of Brooklyn.
Bridge, released by Blues Traveler in May 2001, was the band's first album following the 1999 death of bassist Bobby Sheehan.
Fra Lippo Lippi is an 1855 dramatic monologue written by the Victorian poet Robert Browning, which first appeared in his collection Men and Women.
In Fra Lippo Lippi, Robert Browning depicts a 15th-century real-life painter, Filippo Lippi, and asks whether art should be true to life or an idealized image of life.
Robert Browning's dramatic monologue Fra Lippo Lippi is written in blank verse, which is non-rhyming iambic pentameter.
Castle Sinclair Girnigoe is located about 3 miles north of Wick on the east coast of Caithness, Scotland, and is considered to be one of the earliest seats of Clan Sinclair.
Castle Sinclair Girnigoe comprises the ruins of two castles: the 15th-century Castle Girnigoe and the early 17th-century Castle Sinclair.
Kinnaird Castle is a 15th-century castle located in Angus, Scotland, that has been home to the Carnegie family, the Earl of Southesk, for more than 600 years.
The Carnegie family, the Earl of Southesk, has made Kinnaird Castle in Angus, Scotland, its home for more than 600 years, making the castle a long-standing family seat.
Hayashi castle, also known as Hayashi-jo or Fukuyama-jo, was a 15th-century mountain-type castle in Satoyamabe village, Matsumoto city, Nagano, Japan, and is now largely in ruins.
The Hayashi castle site is sometimes regarded as one castle, or as two castles, Hayashikojo (the small castle) and Hayashiohjo (the larger castle).
Dundas Castle is a 15th-century castle with substantial 19th-century additions by William Burn, located in the Dalmeny parish of West Lothian, Scotland.
Dundas Castle was the home of the Dundas family since the Middle Ages, until it was sold in the late 19th century.
Dundas Castle is currently the residence of politician and businessman Sir Jack Stewart-Clark, in the Dalmeny parish of West Lothian.
Leskovec Castle, also called Turn Castle, is a 15th-century castle north of the village of Leskovec pri Krskem in the Municipality of Krsko, southeastern Slovenia.
Leskovec Castle is known in Slovene as Grad Turn and Grad Leskovec, and in German as Thurn am Hart, and it was redesigned in the 16th and 18th centuries.
Crayke Castle is a grade I listed 15th-century castle in Crayke, North Yorkshire, England, situated on Church Hill in the village of Crayke.
Crayke Castle consists of a restored 15th-century four storey tower house with attached outbuildings to the rear, and a separate ruined 15th-century tower called the New Tower.
Lady Charlotte Elliot, born Charlotte Carnegie, was a Victorian poet who lived from 22 July 1839 to 15 January 1880.
Lady Charlotte Elliot was born on 22 July 1839 in the parish of Farnell, Angus, Scotland, possibly at Kinnaird Castle.
Kilmory Castle, also called Kilmorie Castle or Crowner's Castle, is the remains of a 15th-century castle at Meikle Kilmory on the Isle of Bute, Scotland.
Kilmory Castle was the residence of the Jamiesons of Kilmorie, who were the hereditary coroners of Bute, and it was already a ruin in the 18th century.
The ruins of Kilmory Castle on the Isle of Bute are classified as a secular listed building.
Megginch Castle is a 15th-century castle in Perth and Kinross, in central Scotland, and was the family home of the late Cherry Drummond, 16th Baroness Strange.
Megginch Castle is now occupied by Lady Strange's daughter, Catherine Star Violetta Herdman, and her husband.
The Battle of Berlin, designated the Berlin Strategic Offensive Operation by the Soviet Union, was the final major offensive of the European theatre of World War II.
The Soviet Union designated the Battle of Berlin as the Berlin Strategic Offensive Operation, and it is recorded as the last major offensive of the European theatre of World War II.
Anatoly Iosifovich Petrakovsky (28 December 1901 to 3 September 1969) was a Ukrainian Soviet Army major general and Hero of the Soviet Union.
Anatoly Iosifovich Petrakovsky joined the Red Army in 1922, rose through the ranks to become an officer, and on the eve of the Winter War was a battalion commander in the 13th Rifle Division.

Anatoly Iosifovich Petrakovsky was awarded the title Hero of the Soviet Union and the Order of Lenin for his leadership of the battalion, and after Operation Barbarossa he became commander of the 395th Rifle Division.

Anatoly Iosifovich Petrakovsky led the 395th Rifle Division during the Battle of Rostov and the Battle of Voronezh but was relieved of command due to a systemic failure to comply with orders. In August 1943 he became commander of the 57th Rifle Corps, lost that command, and was sent to hospital for an illness.

After graduating from the Military Academy of the General Staff, Anatoly Iosifovich Petrakovsky was appointed deputy commander of 16th Army and took part in the Invasion of South Sakhalin, and he retired in 1956 after postwar staff positions.
Boris Alexandrovich Vladimirov (14 April 1905 to 1 May 1978) was a Soviet Army lieutenant general and a Hero of the Soviet Union.
Boris Alexandrovich Vladimirov was drafted into the Red Army in 1921, served in the Russian Civil War, and by 1941 had become an officer and was a deputy regimental commander.

After the German invasion of the Soviet Union, Boris Alexandrovich Vladimirov led the formation of march battalions in the Siberian Military District, served as chief of staff of a ski brigade and a rifle brigade, and commanded that rifle brigade in the Siege of Leningrad, the Lyuban Offensive Operation and the Sinyavino Offensive.
Boris Alexandrovich Vladimirov took command of the 311th Rifle Division in March 1943 and was awarded the title Hero of the Soviet Union for his leadership in the Vistula-Oder Offensive.
After the war Boris Alexandrovich Vladimirov became a lieutenant general, commanded a rifle corps, and was deputy chief of staff of the Soviet airborne, and he retired in 1960 and lived in Moscow.
Alexander Petrovich Nikolayev (14 November 1918 to 13 June 2009) was a Red Army senior lieutenant and Hero of the Soviet Union.
Alexander Petrovich Nikolayev received the title Hero of the Soviet Union and the Order of Lenin for his actions during the Battle of Berlin, and he also fought in the Siege of Leningrad.
Mikhail Nikiforovich Linnik (25 October 1916 to 21 December 2007) was a Soviet Army captain and Hero of the Soviet Union.
Mikhail Nikiforovich Linnik was awarded the title Hero of the Soviet Union and the Order of Lenin for his actions during the Lublin-Brest Offensive in September 1944.
Stepan Fyodorovich Shutov (30 January 1902 to 17 April 1963) was a Red Army colonel and double Hero of the Soviet Union.
Stepan Fyodorovich Shutov fought in the Russian Civil War and the Polish-Soviet War, was demobilized after recovering from typhus in 1921, and was drafted into the Red Army again in 1924.

When Germany invaded the Soviet Union, Stepan Fyodorovich Shutov was a tank battalion commander who fought in the Battle of Moscow; in December 1941 he became deputy commander of a tank brigade, and in August 1942 he commanded the 187th Tank Brigade of the 9th Tank Corps.

Stepan Fyodorovich Shutov was awarded the title Hero of the Soviet Union for leading the 20th Guards Tank Brigade in the Battle of Kiev (1943), and received the title a second time for the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive, during which the brigade captured Ploiesti.

Stepan Fyodorovich Shutov was seriously wounded in September 1944, which resulted in the amputation of his arm, retired in September 1945, and later became deputy minister for social welfare of the Belorussian SSR.
Vladimir Fedorovich Vladimirov (9 July 1914 to December 1943) was a Red Army lieutenant during World War II and a Hero of the Soviet Union.

Vladimir Fedorovich Vladimirov was posthumously awarded the title Hero of the Soviet Union and the Order of Lenin for his actions during the Battle of the Dnieper, and he was killed in action in December 1943.
